statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 13% while Stress remains elevated at 54%; the Nasdaq-100 is trading a genuinely two-sided monthly-expiry Friday against a long-end bond market close to two-decade yield highs.
recommendation: Conditions are consistent with functioning mean reversion: the session has already produced a full round trip and repeated retracements in both directions, and implied volatility is decaying into the close. A narrow evidence-based caution window is carried at 19:00Z-20:00Z, where August monthly options expiry concentrates closing and roll flow into the cash close. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Two-sided into expiry: the Nasdaq-100 round-tripped its open, printed 29,405.12 and handed part of it back, leaving retracements working in both directions against a 4.74% 10-year.
body:
Cash NDX trades near 29,302.30, about +0.31% against a 29,213.17 prior close. The session opened at 29,359.60, was faded to a 29,142.44 low, reclaimed the entire decline to a 29,405.12 high and has since given back roughly a hundred points to sit mid-range; NQ September futures are near 29,410.75, about +0.38%, inside a 29,220.75-29,539.00 range against a 29,300.50 prior close and roughly 128 points below their own high. That sequence is the central Tail evidence: extensions are being retraced in both directions rather than compounding after failed pullbacks, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path that overwhelms mean reversion. Volatility agrees, with VIX at 14.89, down 6.0% on the day and printing session lows inside a 14.77-15.95 range.

The stress side of the ledger stays genuinely elevated and is almost entirely a rates story. The 10-year yield is 4.74%, up about 3.0bp, the 2-year 4.24%, up 3.6bp, and the 30-year 5.28%, up 2.4bp and still close to the level that marked its highest since 2007 earlier this week. Reporting today notes that the long end has given back almost all of the relief that followed the Treasury's announcement that it would at least double buybacks of 10-, 20- and 30-year debt, an operation that only begins on September 9. Yesterday's yield rebound triggered a broad equity selloff and today's tape is the rebound from it, with the week still on course for a decline. Gold's 2.5% latest-session advance sits alongside that as the clearest cross-asset expression of duration and debasement concern.

Today's macro is already behind the market. The S&P Global flash PMIs printed at 13:45Z with services at 56.8, the composite at 56.0 and manufacturing at 53.2 against a 53.9 consensus, the strongest activity readings in years and precisely the growth strength that keeps the long end heavy. Price discovery since the release has been orderly and two-sided, which is the observation that matters more than the surprise itself. Internals are split rather than aligned: megacaps are firm on a latest-session basis, led by TSLA, GOOGL and META, while semiconductors are mostly lower with ARM, INTC and MU heavy. That conflict reduces directional conviction and lifts Stress; under this framework it does not lift Tail.

The one narrow forward checkpoint is August monthly options expiry, which concentrates closing and roll flow into the 20:00Z cash close. A caution window is carried at 19:00Z-20:00Z for that reason alone, as a scheduled-flow checkpoint rather than an observed structure, and it releases at the close. From 21:00Z CME equity index futures halt for the weekend, so the later published hours describe a market with no tradable path rather than a forecast of benign structure. Next week's asymmetry sits on Wednesday, where Core PCE, the second-estimate GDP print and NVIDIA results land in one session, ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote on Friday.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: ten hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z and 11:00Z through 16:00Z) and the remaining fourteen clock-hours, covering the whole of the August 20 US afternoon and evening plus scattered overnight gaps, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours the published Tail held a narrow 12-16 band and the mapped policy state was green throughout. The shape is informative: Tail sat at 12 through the Asian and European hours with Stress easing from 59 to 54 as the overnight tape stayed orderly, then stepped up to 15-16 across the 13:00Z-14:00Z flash-PMI and US-open window with the dominant mode briefly published as event/whipsaw. Since the release, Tail has come back down to 14 and then 13 and the mode has returned to mixed, which is the signature of an event that was absorbed rather than one that started a trend. Confidence improved steadily from 83 to 88 as live cash, futures, volatility and rate evidence became available through the European and US mornings.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the current hour at a low Tail while the observed two-way structure continues to be confirmed, then eases through the final cash hour on the assumption that retracements keep appearing on both sides and that long-end yields do not accelerate. One watch-level hour is carried at 19:00Z, where August monthly options expiry concentrates closing and roll flow into the 20:00Z cash close; that elevation is a scheduled-flow checkpoint rather than an observed structure and it releases immediately afterwards. From 21:00Z the published horizon changes character entirely: CME equity index futures halt for the weekend, so every subsequent slot describes a market with no tradable price path. Tail collapses into the low single digits there because the pathological path this score measures requires a live market, and Stress steps down to a floor that represents the standing rate backdrop rather than a live condition. Confidence decays gradually across the weekend with distance from the last observed print. Weekend headline risk, including a US-Canada tariff deadline reported for tonight and continuing energy-supply developments, is carried as reopen gap risk beyond this horizon rather than as current-hour Tail, and next week's concentration of Core PCE, second-estimate GDP and NVIDIA results on Wednesday ahead of Friday's Jackson Hole keynote is treated as a Stress and dispersion consideration only.

Retracements are working in both directions and VIX 14.89 is at session lows, so Tail stays low while Stress reflects a 4.74% 10-year.
